title: How Dagobert Renouf sold $8K of a Twitter course in 24 hours with pain-first positioning
summary: Dagobert explains how he grew a startup audience on Twitter by sharing his journey instead of promoting his product, then used the same emotional playbook to launch a crowded-niche course. He covers aggressive positioning, a pain-to-relief sales page, building the product after the landing page, and researching pains instead of ideas.

principles.text: Share your journey instead of pitching your product; it's relatable to your target audience and drives far more engagement.
principles.quote: to grow on Twitter that it was better to not promote myself and to instead by talking about my journey

principles.text: Emotion is what produces engagement and action, so optimize content for emotional connection over direct promotion.
principles.quote: most important thing is the emotion that's how you get engagement that's how you get action

principles.text: Humor builds instant trust, creating personal-feeling connections at scale that make later conversion easier.
principles.quote: by making someone laugh you just instantly make them trust you

principles.text: In a saturated market, take a risky, polarizing stance so people notice and click through, then let the landing page convince them.
principles.quote: I'd rather call it dominate so even people who think they hate it will check the landing page and then the landing page will convince them

principles.text: Structure the sales page as pain, then absolution (it's not your fault), then the solution.
principles.quote: focus on the pain and then oh but it's not your fault here's the solution

principles.text: Write the landing page story first, then build the product to deliver that promise; it boosts reviews and word of mouth.
principles.quote: it's not like I had my course and then I tried to tell a story about it it's like I had this perfect story and then based on the perfect story I was like okay these are the chapters
